title: Hits and refusing to pay Moe Gale fifty percent
summary: Cherry Red Blues and Things Ain't What They Used to Be made him successful; he stopped paying fifty percent and bookings dropped.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well, now, let me tell you. So I wasn't doing nothing. So the next year, I think I made
You did?
Yeah.
(Laughter)
How come?
Huh?
How come? You had these hit records.
I had "Cherry Red Blues", yeah. And "Things Ain't What They Used to Be". And they didn't squeeze me out. I got in all the major theaters cross country. And I played everything.
Well, Cootie, let me get this straight now. Now, just a minute. So was this your first year with Mo Gale? Or second year with Mo Gale.
This was my first year with Mo Gale.
So he was in on fifty percent of that?
He was in on fifty percent of that. So after I'd made all this money, I go to Mo Gale and tell him, I said, "Man, I can't give you fifty percent of my earnings."
(Laughter)
So I stopped giving him fifty percent.
Well, were you tied up? Did you have a contract?
There's no contract you can make with a man to get fifty percent of your earnings. So I knew that.
Oh, good. Yeah.
And so now, I'm mighty well established see, and I'm rolling on. The next year I make $150,000.00. So I started to going down. And sure as shooting, it's a control on that business.
You mean, those are going to make money where they're going to make money.
Yeah.
And if they don't have that much percentage in it, there isn't that much work being done on it.
Right.
Well, could you see the difference in the bookings?
Oh, yeah.
Is that right.
Soon as I started giving up that fifty percent, I could see the difference in the bookings.
